caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 43 of 1979.
lawyer:
SM Monir, Advocate ----- For the Appellants.
BK Das, Advocate ----- For Respondent No. 1
parties:
Shah Alam and others   ----- Appellants.
Vs.
Masuma Khatoon and others ----- Respondent.
full_judgment: 13. Now coming to the evidence of possession of the plaintiffs it is seen that PW 1 Syed Nuruddin Wahed Ali, husband of plaintiff No.2 has deposed in support of the plaintiffs' exclusive possession of the suit plot. He stated that the plaintiffs possessed the suit plot through their borgader Sultan Mia who at a subsequent stage executed a borga kabuliyat Ext. 3 in their favour and after him plaintiffs possessed through their borgader PW 6 Md. Tayeb Ali who executed borga Kabuliyat Exts. 3(a) to 3(c). He further stated that the plaintiffs paid rent from 1367 BS up to 1386 BS by mutating their names vide rent receipts Ext. 4 series. PW 1 is corroborated in respect of plaintiffs exclusive possession of the suit plot by a neighboring resident PW 2 Azharul Islam who is a retired Government servant. PW 6 Md. Tayeb Ali also corroborated the PW 1. PW 3 Mansur Ali who had a piece of land to the north of the suit plot and which he sold 8/9 years before and who is a resident of the locality stated that he saw Kadam Ali to possess the entire suit plot and defendant No. 1 had been possessing 10 or 11 decimals in the suit plot by sing a hut for the last 2 and 2½ years and prior to that PW 1 and his bhaira possessed the entire suit plot and the defendants did not possess any portion of the suit plot prior to 2 or 2½ years of course he stated in cross-examination that he saw sons of Kadam Ali to possess along with their father without stating the time. It must be before his sale of the land to Azizur Rahman. It is but natural for the sons to help their father in cultivatting the land. That does not mean their independent possession and the same is clear from his denial of defendants suggestion that the plaintiffs possessed 4½ pakhis in the east and the rest 1.14 acre in the west in the suit pot. PW 4, Kazi Fakhruddin Ahmed, a retired government servant and a surveyor measured the suit plot and prepared the map attached to plaintiffs' Kabalas Ext. 2(a) and 2(b) on the identification of husband of plaintiff No. 1. PW 5 Lal Mia who resides 500 feet away from the suit plot clearly stated in his deposition that he saw Kadam Ali to possess the entire suit plot. 'He further stated that while.in possession Kadam Ali sold it to one Azizur Rahman who sold to the plaintiffs who possessed through Sultan and at present Tyeb Ali has been possessing on plaintiffs behalf. But this witness also stated that 5/6 years after purchase by the plaintiffs sons of Kadam Ali possessed some portion in the western part of the plot. Relying upon this the learned Advocate for the appellants strenuously contended that the defendants Sifo and Julmat Ali possessed from western part of the suit plot as claimed by them on the basis of amicable arrangement with Kadam Ali From the cross-examination of DW 1 Almat Ali defendant No. 10) it is seen that the defendants 8 and 10 received compensation for 0.24 acres of land of plot No. 371 of their kabala land in LA case No. 41 of 1964-65 in which case plot Nos. 365 and 371 were acquired. This goes to show that PW 5 meant to say that sons of Kadam Ali were in possession in the land of plot No. 371 and not in the suit plot. This portion of the deposition of PW 5 inconsistent with his earlier statement in his deposition appears to us not to have been correctly recorded Almat Ali is defendant No. 10 and ow 3 Sirajul Huq son-in-law of Kadam Ali is defendant No.6. He also attested the sale deed executed' by Kadam Ali in favour of Azizur Rahman vendor' of the plaintiffs. They being interested in the result of the suit they cannot be relied upon without 'independent corroboration. DW 2 Haji Kala Chand Mia who claims to be a resident of Agargaon and an old man of 95 years is an over zealous witness. He stated that defendant No. 10 was 40 years-old at the time of Kabala Ext. B(1) whereas defendant No. 10 himself as OW 1 admitted that he was only 14/15 years old at 'that time. He also stated that defendant No. 1 is a Municipal Commissioner but denied the suggestion that he came to depose falsely to please him DW 4 Ali Mia who also claims to be a resident of Agargaon is another over zealous witness. He stated that Kadam Ali sold the eastern part and still owned western part of the suit plot though he stated on recall that he did not say that Kadam Ali possesses the western portion still now. How could sons of Kadam Ali possess their entire purchased 0.73 acres from plot No: 313 as deposed by DWs when as admitted by DW 1 that they received compensation for requisition and acquisition of plot No. 371? The statement of the Dws. that defendant Nos. 8,10 and Julmat Ali constructed the straw hut is belied by the recital in the kabalas Ext. B(2) and B(3) in favour of principal defendant Nos. 1-6 inasmuch as there is no mention of such straw hut in the said deeds. Therefore, it is difficult to rely upon the testimony of the said DWs contrary to recital in their sale deeds. In view of the above discussion of evidence record we are of the view that Kadam Ali had been in sole possession of the suit plot No. 313 till his sale in 1957 to Mohammad Azizur Rahman vendor of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs got possession from him of the said land after their purchase in 1958 and the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the entire suit plot till their dispossession of the 'B' schedule land measuring 0'10 acres on 9.2.76.
